MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 24, 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins (arrived at 5:07 p.m.); Mayor Pro Tern Bruce
  Silverstein; and Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad (arrived at 5:03 p.m.), Doug Stewart
  and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Anne K declined the opportunity to speak.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:02 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Personnel Matters pursuant to Government Code Section 54957:

  1.  Public Employee Appointment
  Title: City Manager

Conference with Labor Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6:

  1.  City representative: Interim City Attorney Trevor Rusin
  Unrepresented employee: City Manager

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  1.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (2)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Riggins called the meeting to order at 5:45 p.m.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 2 of 13

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Marianne Riggins; Mayor Pro Tern Bruce Silverstein; and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Doug Stewart and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Candace Bond, Interim City
  Manager; Richard Rojas, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Yolanda
  Bundy, Community Development Director; Susan Duefias, Public Safety Director; Rob
  DuBoux, Public Works Director; Frances Arricale, Deputy City Manager; Adam
  Pisarkiewicz, Contract Planner; Luis Flores, Senior Management Analyst; Brandie Ayala,
  Senior Management Analyst; Parker Davis, Media Technician; and Jason Lawrence,
  Deputy City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Sections
  54957, 54957.6, and 54956.9(d)(4), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the
  Council discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Riggins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for this meeting was properly posted on
  November 14, 2025, with the first amended agenda posted on November 20, 2025. The
  second amended agenda was properly posted at City Hall on November 24 at 4:30 p.m.,
  but due to a technical issue the website agenda posting linked to the first amended agenda.
  The supporting materials for the new items, Item Nos. 1.B.8., 1.B.9., and 7.D., were
  available on the website at the time of posting. Once staff noticed the error, the link to the
  second amended agenda was corrected and a notification was sent to all email and text
  subscribers at 6:14 p.m. on November 24, 2025. In addition to the agenda posting, a
  supplemental report was posted for Item 5.B. on November 21, 2025 at 4:53 p.m. and
  second supplemental report for that item was posted at 6:14 p.m.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved to approve the agenda and pull Item No. 1.B.7. from
  the Consent Calendar.

  The Council discussed the motion.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 3 of 13

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved to hear Item No. 5.B. as soon as possible after
  6:30 p.m. and continue Item No. 8.C. to the December 8, 2025 Regular Meeting.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein second the motion.

  The motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion
  to continue Item No. 7.C. The motion failed, 2-3, Councilmember Uhring,
  Councilmember Stewart, and Mayor Riggins opposed

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Riggins opened the floor to public comment.

  Justin was not available at the time of the hearing.

  As there were no other speakers present for the Consent Calendar, the Mayor
  returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  Item No. 1.B.7. was pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item No. 1.B.7. The motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  1.  Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 529
  Recommended Action: Conduct second reading, unless waived, and adopt
  Ordinance No. 529, amending Malibu Municipal Code Sections 2.56.070,
  2.56.110, and 2.56.12, increasing the City Manager's purchasing authority
  from $25,000 to $60,000 and raising the small purchase/open-market
  purchases procedure from $5,000 to $10,000 in line with rate of inflation.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive
  full reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on
  first reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  77166-77298 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 779 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 4 of 13

  of $4,346,090.95. City of Malibu payroll check number 5534-5537 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $549,737.11.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 27, 2025 Regular
  Meeting.
  4.  Investment Report for the Month Ending October 31, 2025
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending October 31, 2025.
  5.  Acceptance of Clover Heights Avenue Storm Drain Improvements Project
  Recommended Action: 1) Accept the work performed by J. Vega
  Engineering, Inc. for the Clover Heights Storm Drain Improvements
  Project, Specification No. 2101 as complete; and 2) Authorize the Public
  Works Director to submit for recordation a Notice of Completion.
  6.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding Conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 25-54 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency related to the increase of
  reckless and illegal driving on pacific coast highway and directing staff to
  coordinate efforts with other governmental agencies to increase attention
  and create programs to reduce the risk and danger associated with Pacific
  Coast Highway in the City.
  8.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding the Palisades Fire
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 25-58, extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency in response to the
  Palisades Fire.
  9.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding the Franklin Fire
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 25-59, extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency in response to the Franklin
  Fire.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  7.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency and Continuing a Program for Reducing the Risk of Fires
  Associated with Individuals Engaged in Unpermitted Camping
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 25-55 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency and continuing a program
  for reducing the risk of fires associated with individuals engaged in
  unpermitted camping.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a
  motion to adopt Resolution No. 25-55, adding Section 2(4) City staff is
  directed to work with LASD to remove all individuals engaged in
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 5 of 13

  unpermitted camping in any and all areas designated as VHFHZ in Malibu.
  If necessary to accomplish this object, such individuals should be arrested
  and prosecuted to the fullest extent permissible by law," extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency and continuing a program
  for reducing the risk of fires associated with individuals engaged in
  unpermitted camping. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Interim City Manager Bond expressed Thanksgiving gratitude for the resiliency of
  the Malibu community and dedicated City staff. She provided an update on
  continued negotiations for school separation agreements and announced the
  agreements would be considered by the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School
  District Board of Education on December 1, 2025. She provided an update on
  Southern California Edison (SCE) undergrounding in the Palisades Fire area and
  support from SCE for City, SM-MUSD, and Caltrans projects. She announced a
  Los Angeles County initiative to coordinate undergrounding telecom lines in
  addition to electric lines. She reported the City has submitted a FEMA hazard
  mitigation grant application to underground telecom lines in the Palisades Fire burn
  area. She announced an Executive Order from the Governor that will allow
  homeowners rebuilding from the Palisades Fire to use insurance proceeds for
  optional solar and other environmental updates, suspend certain State statutes to
  support quick development of municipal sewer systems, and expand protections to
  prioritize those displaced by the Palisades Fire on waitlists for affordable housing.
  She announced Dick Van Dyke's 100th birthday on December 13, 2026 and
  associated celebrations in Malibu. She encouraged the public to take the evacuation
  plan survey to help with development of the evacuation plan update. She discussed
  recent and upcoming Environmental Health programs and events.. She encouraged
  business owners to take the Business Recovery and Resilience survey. She
  announced the Malibu Education Foundation annual holiday tree lot and
  Thanksgiving holiday hours for City facilities.

  Community Development Director Bundy provided a fire rebuild update. She
  reported on rebuild statistics and Executive Order N-37-25. She announced
  upcoming community sessions, including a design professionals meeting, a
  geotechnical workshop, and community meetings with rebuild families.

  The Council directed questions to Community Development Director Bundy.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, presented
  annual crime statistics for 2025 and reviewed the Lost Hills-Malibu station
  operations in 2025 and plans for 2026.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 6 of 13

  The Council directed questions to Sergeant Soderlund.

RECESS  At 6:27 p.m., Mayor Riggins recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:37
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  B.  Appeal of Planning Commission Resolution No. 25-69 Regarding Coastal

  new or upgraded curb ramps, 6,956 linear feet of new sidewalks, three new
  retaining walls, two realigned intersections, 27 new light poles, 9.7 miles of new or
  upgraded bike lanes, a vehicle pull-out for law enforcement use, median
  reconstruction at various locations, and associated roadway improvements along
  Pacific Coast Highway within the Public Right-of-Way (Citywide, along Pacific
  Coast Highway within the Public Right-of-Way from Serra Road to the Ventura
  County border, Owner: California Department of Transportation; Appellant:
  Malibu Township Council)
  Recommended Action: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 25-57 Determining the Project Is
  Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act, Denying Appeal No. 25-
  007, and Approving Coastal Development Permit No. 25-009 for the Installation of
  19 New Guardrails, 22 New or Upgraded Curb Ramps, 6,956 Linear Feet of New

  Way Between the Ventura County Line and Serra Road (California Department of

  continue Item No. 7.C. to the December 8, 2025 Regular Meeting.

  The motion carried, 4-0, with Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein absent.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein returned to the dais at 9:37 p.m.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Andrew Vznis and Parker Kaplan announced the opening of the Malibu Education
  Foundation community tree lot, thanked Council for fee waiver for the event, and
  discussed students' roles in the tree lot operations.

  Kevin Keegan declined the opportunity to.speak.

  Norm Haynie discussed the Council's dedicated efforts to move fire rebuilds
  forward.

  Annestacia K declined the opportunity to speak.

  Darren Graves deferred time to Danny Smith.

  Arno Koch deferred time to Danny Smith.

  Jo Drummond deferred time to Danny Smith.

  Danny Smith discussed requirements to replace septic tanks and the Regional Water
  Quality Control Boards' interpretation of "failure", which would require all onsite
  wastewater management (OWTS) systems to be replaced by advanced OWTS
  systems on properties damaged by the Palisades Fire, and the burden it would create
  for property owners.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Mr. Smith stated a sewer would be the best
  environmental option.

  Scott Dittrich discussed the streamlined process to apply for and receive his
  electrical permit. He discussed the temporary 25-mph speed limit in the fire burn
  area despite the lack of construction. He stated the City needed a permanent City
  Manager and he recommended considering Glen Becerra.

  Councilmember Uhring stated he had received positive feedback about the reduced
  speed limit.

  Salwa Wahba was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Josh Spiegel was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Bill Sampson was not present at the time of the hearing.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 9 of 13

  Pamela Conley Ulich was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Lee Haber, Caltrans, thanked the Council for approving Coastal Development
  Permit (CDP) No. 25-009. He announced a public meeting the following Tuesday
  at City Hall on PCH roundabouts.

  Thomas Spencer discussed Planning Commissioner John Ma77a s 16 years of
  service and expressed concern about his political integrity. . He discussed Jo
  Drummond's appeal of Coastal Development Permit No. 25-009 and expressed
  concern that it put the City in jeopardy. He discussed the Malibu Township
  Council's (MTC) appeals of development projects and reporting of code
  enforcement violations.

  Dustan Batton discussed MTC's role in local politics and its activities. He stated
  the MTC did not represent the community.

  Andy Lyon discussed the removal of the temporary skatepark.

  Nino discussed a community petition in support of Glen Becerra for City Manager.

  Ryan discussed improvements needed to improve PCH safety on the east side of
  the City. He indicated support for widening the road to protect pedestrians.

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Uhring encouraged remote speakers criticizing MTC to participate
  in the meetings in-person. He commended Public Works staff for their response to
  recent storms. He stated he had attended some Rebuild Zone Captains meetings
  and encouraged the public to submit their rebuild applications.

  Councilmember Conrad questions about whether construction is ongoing on PCH.
  She indicated agreement that the City needed a permanent City Manager. She
  stated skaters were temporarily displaced while the skate park was under
  construction and could still skate at other locations in neighboring cities. She
  discussed the costs of appeals in time and money for the City and thanked the
  Council for approving the Caltrans project.

  Councilmember Stewart stated he attended event at Topanga regarding Los
  Angeles County and Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA) fire
  and land management plans. He discussed the innovations in the program.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein, Public Works Director Duboux
  discussed the construction timeline for the permanent skatepark and impacts from
  the recent rains. He stated he was confident the skatepark would be open by the
  end of February, although some elements may still be being completed.

  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein discussed how the 25-mph speed limit demonstrated
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of November 24, 2025
  Page 10 of 13

  that lower speed limits could improve public safety. He indicated support for taking
  a position on the Regional Water Quality Control Boards' interpretation. He stated
  he met with Glen Becerra and was impressed by him but expressed concern a city
  Manager candidate would solicit support from the residents. He encouraged remote
  speakers criticizing MTC to participate in the meetings in-person. He stated
  appeals were important and he learned a lot through the public hearings.

  Mayor Riggins stated the City had retained a recruitment firm to conduct the City
  Manager recruitment and that candidates could apply through that process. She
  commended City staff for their work throughout the year and encouraged the public
  to shop locally on Small Business Saturday after Thanksgiving.

  Councilmember Uhring commended Interim City Manager Bond for her service.

  The Council discussed reordering the agenda.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tern Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart 'seconded a motion

  C.  Amendment to the Malibu Local Coastal Program and Malibu Municipal Code
  Title 17 (Zoning) Modifying Standards Related to Beachfront Total Development
  Square Footage and Establishing a Beachfront Definition
  Recommended Action: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 25-56 initiating amendments to
  the Local Coastal Program (LCP) and Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal
  Code (MMC) modifying standards related to beachfront total development square
  footage (TDSF), clarifying the definition of beachfront lots, and addressing related
